<thought>Based on the ¹H NMR spectrum, there are four distinct signals corresponding to four unique hydrogen environments: a singlet for 3 H (likely OCH₃), a 1 H aromatic signal at 7.49 ppm, a 9 H aromatic signal at 7.66 ppm, and a 1 H aromatic signal at 8.39 ppm. Hence, the number of chemically equivalent hydrogen types is 4.</thought>
<final_answer>4</final_answer>
